title: Module 4 intro — Cluster Test and Verification

lines: Welcome to Module Four: Cluster Test and Verification.
It's where you prove a new cluster is healthy before anyone trusts it with real work.
Picture a brand-new 256-GPU cluster handed straight to researchers, with no burn-in.
Their first big training run crawls, far slower than the specs promised.

say.0: Picture a brand-new two hundred fifty-six G P U cluster handed straight to researchers, with no burn-in.

lines: The culprit: one node's all-reduce bandwidth is half that of its peers.
A swapped rail cable and a transceiver on old firmware drag every step down.
Then, two hours into a long run, one GPU starts throwing errors under load.
The job crashes, and a week of cluster time disappears into finger-pointing.

say.0: Then, two hours into a long run, one G P U starts throwing errors under load.

lines: Every one of these faults was findable before handover.
Systematic testing, from a single node up to the whole fabric, would have caught them all.
Lesson one starts on a single node, with DCGM diagnostics run through dcgmi.
The longer diagnostic levels stress every GPU and flag memory, power, and thermal problems.

say.0: Lesson one starts on a single node, with D C G M diagnostics run through D C G M I.
say.1: The longer diagnostic levels stress every G P U and flag memory, power, and thermal problems.

lines: Then comes HPL, the dense linear-algebra benchmark behind the TOP500 list.
A short run checks performance, and hours of HPL burn-in expose GPUs that fail under heat.

say.0: Then comes H P L, the dense linear-algebra benchmark behind the top five hundred list.
say.1: A short run checks performance, and hours of H P L burn-in expose G P Us that fail under heat.

lines: Lesson two turns to NCCL, the library that moves data between GPUs.
Its all-reduce tests measure NVLink Switch bandwidth inside each node.

say.0: Lesson two turns to nickel, the library that moves data between G P Us.
say.1: Its all-reduce tests measure en-vee-link Switch bandwidth inside each node.

lines: Across nodes, the same tests measure east-west fabric bandwidth.
A slow node stands out immediately, and long runs become a fabric burn-in.
Lesson three validates cabling and signal quality.
You'll confirm every cable lands in the right port, then read link errors and the bit error rate, or BER.

say.1: You'll confirm every cable lands in the right port, then read link errors and the bit error rate, or B E R.

lines: Lesson four confirms firmware and software versions everywhere.
Switches, BlueField-3 DPUs, and even transceivers must match the approved baseline.

say.1: Switches, BlueField three D P Us, and even transceivers must match the approved baseline.

lines: Lesson five brings in ClusterKit, which runs a battery of health and performance checks across the cluster.
It compares every node against its peers, so outliers can't hide.
A NeMo burn-in then trains a real model across the cluster for hours.
It's the closest thing to the researchers' actual workload.

say.0: A Neemo burn-in then trains a real model across the cluster for hours.

lines: Storage gets tested too, with read and write throughput benchmarks.
Slow storage starves GPUs just as surely as a bad cable does.

say.1: Slow storage starves G P Us just as surely as a bad cable does.

lines: Run it all, and the cluster reaches researchers at full speed.
Every result is saved as a baseline for troubleshooting later.
This is the largest domain: thirty-three percent, a third of the exam.
Lesson one starts on a single node, with stress tests and HPL.

say.1: Lesson one starts on a single node, with stress tests and H P L.
